clinical_category: Inflammatory arthritis - rheumatoid arthritis versus osteoarthritis pattern recognition
blueprint_topic: Differentiation of inflammatory and degenerative joint disease manifestations
stem: A client reports 3 months of pain and swelling in both wrists and several finger joints, morning stiffness lasting about 90 minutes that improves with movement, and persistent fatigue. Which interpretation by the nurse is most accurate?

options.A: The pattern is more consistent with rheumatoid arthritis because the joint involvement is symmetric and inflammatory, with prolonged morning stiffness and systemic symptoms.
options.B: The pattern is more typical of osteoarthritis because osteoarthritis usually causes prolonged morning stiffness and symmetric inflammatory swelling of small joints.
options.C: Rheumatoid arthritis is unlikely because it does not cause fatigue or symptoms outside a single weight-bearing joint.
options.D: The pattern excludes inflammatory arthritis because morning stiffness that improves with movement occurs only with mechanical joint disease.

rationale: A is correct. Current American College of Rheumatology guidance describes rheumatoid arthritis as an autoimmune inflammatory arthritis that commonly causes symmetric involvement of small joints in the hands, wrists, and feet, with pain, swelling, stiffness, and morning stiffness that may last more than an hour and improve with movement. NIAMS likewise describes symmetric joint involvement, stiffness after waking or prolonged rest, fatigue, and occasional systemic symptoms, while using a broader threshold of longer than 30 minutes rather than requiring one exact cutoff in every patient. In contrast, NIAMS describes osteoarthritis as a degenerative joint disease in which pain commonly occurs with joint use and may improve with rest, while morning or post-rest stiffness is usually less than 30 minutes. B reverses these characteristic patterns. C is incorrect because fatigue and multijoint symmetric disease are well recognized in RA. D is incorrect because prolonged morning stiffness that improves with activity supports inflammatory rather than purely mechanical disease. The final item uses a symptom cluster rather than treating any single stiffness-duration threshold as independently diagnostic.
educational_objective: Differentiate rheumatoid arthritis from osteoarthritis by recognizing symmetric inflammatory small-joint disease, prolonged morning stiffness that improves with movement, and systemic symptoms such as fatigue.
source_organization: American College of Rheumatology (ACR); National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS)
source_version_date: Current ACR and NIAMS health-information resources accessed 2026-08-18; NIAMS osteoarthritis page last reviewed 2023-09
source_locator: ACR 'Rheumatoid Arthritis' → Signs/Symptoms: symmetric small-joint involvement, morning stiffness lasting more than one hour and improving with movement, persistent inflammatory symptoms. NIAMS 'Rheumatoid Arthritis' → Symptoms: symmetric involvement, pain/swelling/warmth, stiffness lasting longer than 30 minutes after waking/rest and fatigue. NIAMS 'Osteoarthritis' → Symptoms: pain with joint use that may improve with rest and morning/post-rest stiffness usually lasting less than 30 minutes.
source_claim_supported: Current ACR and NIAMS sources directly support the rheumatoid-arthritis symptom pattern used in the stem and distinguish it from the shorter, more mechanical stiffness pattern commonly seen in osteoarthritis without requiring one universal duration cutoff for RA diagnosis.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity → Physiological Adaptation: recognize manifestations and pathophysiology of acute and chronic alterations in body systems and identify clinically meaningful changes requiring further evaluation.
correction_summary: Fresh re-audit of the source's feature-list recall into an applied inflammatory-versus-degenerative arthritis pattern-recognition item. The final version uses the full symptom cluster, acknowledges the ACR/NIAMS difference in stiffness wording, and avoids treating a single duration threshold as universally diagnostic.
audit_findings: The source concept was clinically correct but presented as a direct feature list and overstated a greater-than-one-hour duration as if it were the only acceptable RA stiffness description.

Fresh ACR review supports symmetric small-joint inflammation and morning stiffness often lasting more than an hour, while NIAMS supports prolonged stiffness greater than 30 minutes plus fatigue and symmetry.
NIAMS osteoarthritis guidance independently supports a more mechanical pain pattern and morning/post-rest stiffness usually under 30 minutes.
Distractors test reversed OA/RA patterns, denial of systemic RA manifestations and false mechanical interpretation of prolonged morning stiffness; none is defensible.
